land.text: Dali's land in Yunnan, shape of 947 used from 937

predecessors.note: 'In 937, Duan Siping overthrew the Dayining Kingdom and established the Dali Kingdom' (Yunnan page); the dachanghe dossier covers 902-937. Cliopatria's first Dali shape is 947.

land.text: Dali's land, taken by the Mongols 1253-1256 and made into Yunnan province

successors.note: 'In 1256 Duan Xingzhi surrendered and presented to Mongke maps of Yunnan' (Dali page); the Yuan 'created the province of Yunnan after it occupied the Dali Kingdom' (Yunnan page); the Duan family stayed as local rulers (tusi) until the Ming conquest of Yunnan in the early 1380s.

capitals.name: Yangjumie (Dali)
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Yangjumie, present-day Dali Town, Yunnan. 'Seized power in 937, establishing himself at Dali'. The Mongol columns converged on the city in late 1253; Duan Xingzhi then fled to Shanchan (the Kunming area), so the court was there from 1253 to 1256 (the page gives no coordinates).

rulers.name: Duan Siping
rulers.note: Infobox of the Duan Siping page: reign 937-944 (born 893, died 944 at Dengzhou); founder and first emperor of Dali.

rulers.name: Gao Shengtai
rulers.note: Coup of 1094 (state renamed Dazhong); he 'ruled briefly until his death in 1096, after which the throne returned to the Duan family'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Dali shape is 947, but the Duan Siping page gives his reign as 937-944 and the Dali page has him 'seize power in 937, establishing himself at Dali' (the Yunnan page: 'In 937, Duan Siping overthrew the Dayining Kingdom'). No page opened gives the extent in 937-946, so the 947 shape is carried back (confidence 1 for the extent).

360.6 thousand km2 in Yunnan (98.5-106.3 E, 21.4-29.0 N). The page gives no area and no boundary; it says Dali 'voluntarily established tribute relations in 982' but stayed 'essentially an independent state', and that Song Taizu 'declared the land south of the Dadu River to be Dali territory'. The shape fits both: it holds 99% of Yunnan's size (363 thousand km2 by the gazetteer) with different edges, and its northern edge (28.9 N) is where the Dadu River segment begins. It leaves out about 63 thousand km2 of the west and south of present Yunnan and adds about 27 thousand km2 of southern Sichuan (the Dadu side), 5 thousand of Guizhou, 1.5 thousand each of Guangxi and Vietnam and 1 thousand each of Myanmar and Laos; the page is silent on those edges. Kept.

360.4 thousand km2: the same shape as 947 except three 1-degree cells (about 759 km2, 0.2%) shifted on the south-east edge (99.3-105.8 E, 22.0-23.5 N). No page dates any change on the border; the Song neighbour changes from the Later Shu (conquered 965, to which Dali sent congratulation) to the Song. Kept.

359.8 thousand km2: 1,517 km2 (six 1-degree cells) smaller than 970's shape, which drops a strip of the Guizhou-Guangxi-Yunnan corner (104.6-106.1 E, 23.4-26.1 N); the net area is 0.2% lower. No page dates a gain or loss of land in the 11th century (Cliopatria's row has no attached source for this step). Kept; the Gao Shengtai coup of 1094-1096 changed the ruling family, not the borders.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1250-1255; the state ends in 1256 (Cliopatria: 1259)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps the 1250 shape to 1259, but the page has the Mongol columns converge on the city of Dali 'in late 1253', Duan Xingzhi flee to Shanchan and surrender 'in 1256'; the Yunnan page says the kingdom 'was conquered by the Mongol Empire in 1253 after Dali King Duan Xingzhi defected'. The shape is kept unchanged for 1250-1255 as the contested state (the pages give no front line) and the state ends in 1256.

region.text: Duan Siping's land in Yunnan, round the Erhai lake and Dali

ledger.note: 937: Duan Siping founds the Dali Kingdom. 'Finally Duan Siping seized power in 937 and established the Dali Kingdom' (Nanzhao page); the Dali page: 'Seized power in 937, establishing himself at Dali' (Dali page); 'In 937, Duan Siping overthrew the Dayining Kingdom and established the Dali Kingdom' (Yunnan page). The pages do not give the extent, so the 947 shape stands in (confidence 2). The Dali page dates the Dayining regime 928-937, the Nanzhao page 929-937.
1094: Gao Shengtai seizes the throne and renames the state Dazhong ('coup by Gao Shengtai in 1094'). The page does not say what happened to the land.
1096: the Duan family returns. Gao Shengtai 'ruled briefly until his death in 1096, after which the throne returned to the Duan family' and the Dali name was restored.

region.text: the Erhai plain round the city of Dali, where the Mongol columns converged in late 1253

ledger.note: 1253: the Mongol invasion. 'The kingdom was conquered by the Mongol Empire in 1253 after Dali King Duan Xingzhi defected to the Mongols' (Yunnan page); the Dali page: 'In late 1253, the three columns converged on the city of Dali' (Kublai crossed the Jinsha at night; Duan Xingzhi fled to Shanchan, the Kunming area) and its infobox ends the kingdom in 1253.

region.text: the Erhai plain round Dali, with Shanchan

ledger.note: 1256: Duan Xingzhi surrenders. 'In 1256 Duan Xingzhi surrendered and presented to Mongke maps of Yunnan'; the Mongols 'took Dali and Shanchan' after about two more years of fighting, and Uriyangkhadai set up brigades (Dali page).

region.text: all of Dali, to the Mongol Empire

ledger.note: 1256: the Dali Kingdom ends. Duan Xingzhi surrendered in 1256 and was enfeoffed as Maharaja; 'the Yuan dynasty created the province of Yunnan after it occupied the Dali Kingdom' (Yunnan page); 'The Duans were incorporated into the Mongol administration as Maharajas of the new province' and the Duan remnants lasted until the Ming conquest of Yunnan by the early 1380s. Cliopatria ends the row in 1259; the Dali page's infobox ends the kingdom in 1253.

wars.name: Zhizhi's attack on Dai Viet
wars.outcome: c.1137: Zhizhi with 3,000 Dali troops attacked Ly Anh Tong and was defeated (Dali page; the page says 'c.1137' and gives no front).
wars.note: Cliopatria's Vietnam row for these years is 'Ngo Dynasty' (to 1407), which is why that slug stands for the Ly court here.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of Dali

zones.text: the Erhai plain round Dali and Shanchan

wars.outcome: Mongke put Kublai in charge; three columns, Kublai crossing the Jinsha at night; they converged on the city of Dali in late 1253; Duan Xingzhi fled to Shanchan and surrendered in 1256; Uriyangkhadai set up brigades. He then took Dai Viet's Thang Long in 1258 (Uriyangkhadai page).
wars.note: The Uriyangkhadai page gives no date for the Dali campaign itself.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary of Dali; Cliopatria's shape is carried as drawn (Yunnan plus fringes) and checked only against the Dadu River statement.

sources.title: Dali Kingdom
sources.note: Founding 937, Song tribute 982, Gao Shengtai 1094-1096, Mongol conquest 1253-1256.

sources.title: Nanzhao
sources.note: The Dachanghe, Datianxing and Dayining regimes before 937 and the capital.

sources.title: Yunnan
sources.note: 937 founding, 1253 conquest, Yunnan province under the Yuan, Duan family to the 1380s.

sources.title: Uriyangkhadai
sources.note: Opened for the Dali campaign: the page names Uriyangkhadai and Kublai but dates only the 1257-1258 Dai Viet campaign, so nothing is taken from it for the ledger.

notes:
Cliopatria's Dali row runs 947-1259 in four near-identical shapes (360.6, 360.4, 359.8 and 359.8 thousand km2). The dossier runs 937-1256: Duan Siping founded the state in 937 (ten years before the first shape) and Duan Xingzhi surrendered in 1256 (three years before the row ends). The Dali page's infobox ends the kingdom in 1253 and the Yunnan page says 'conquered ... in 1253 after ... Duan Xingzhi defected'; the Dali page's own text has the surrender in 1256. 1256 is used because the page dates the surrender, with the contest recorded from 1253.

Shape: the pages open give no boundary at all. The Dadu River sentence supports the northern edge (southern Sichuan); the Song relation is nominal ('tributary', 'essentially independent', three court visits), so no vassal events are written (Cliopatria has no relation row for Dali either). The Dachanghe dates differ between pages: Dali page 903/902-927, 927-928, 928-937; Nanzhao page 902-928, 928-929, 929-937 (see the dachanghe dossier). The rulers' list pages did not load; only Duan Siping, Gao Shengtai and Duan Xingzhi are named.
